summary.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.
summary.overview:
Operating revenue was Rs 70.36 crore (+31.34% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 19.8 crore (+62.16%) at a 28.1% margin and PAT of Rs 16.25 crore (+59.31%) at a 22.3% margin, with EPS of Rs 5.07. Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.</overview>

segments.name: Boric acid (technical and IP grade)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from boric acid; IP grade is 7-8% of boric acid volume (about 100 tonnes vs 1,500 tonnes technical, per the speaker). Capacity utilisation expected at 96-98% of practical capacity, with output rising to about 18,000 tonnes this year from 15,917 tonnes last year.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.name: Kronox Lab Sciences (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore planned in phases over 18-24 months, with benefits from FY29 and full impact in FY30-31; management expects 3-3.5x current revenue post-capex.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance Rs 250-260 crore vs Rs 215 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margin about 20% and absolute EBITDA growth of about 11-12%.
Q2 expected to be softer on monsoon-weak volumes and raw material inflation from the ongoing war; margins not expected to match Q1's 28.1%.
Q3 expected to pick up again.
Boron oxide and boric acid capacity additions planned; management expects these to lift margins in FY28.
Capex of about Rs 50 crore over the next two to three years (Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore, boric acid Rs 20-25 crore, plus contingency); the Rs 50 crore figure is a business-plan rounding.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity about 26,000 tonnes per year at Pithampur: about 20,000 tpa boric acid and 6,000 tpa DOT.
Practical output expected at about 18,000 tonnes this year vs 15,917 tonnes last year, after planned maintenance days.
Boron oxide capex about Rs 20 crore; boric acid capex Rs 20-25 crore, with plant size flexible between 5,000 and 20,000 tpa.
Kronox Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore in phases: first phase about Rs 55-60 crore; benefits from FY29, full impact FY30-31; execution 18-24 months.
Management says there is capacity upside of 15-20% at existing Indo Borax plants through process changes.
demand_pricing: Indian boric acid market estimated at about 40,000 tpa, projected to grow about 8% CAGR to about 53,000 tpa by 2030; steel and refractory is 55-60% of demand.

Boric acid prices moved from about Rs 127/kg early in FY27 to about Rs 155-160/kg, per management, as costs rose during the war; some pass-through still pending and spot prices were soft in Q2 seasonally.
Management says Indo Borax prices at a premium to market (market plus), citing specifications.
DOT: management cites about 8,500 tonnes of imports and about 10,000 tonnes total market; Indo Borax targets 1,500 tonnes.
Kronox's Indian market growing about 11% CAGR per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the promoter's reasons. It said the Dahej land and design are ready, audits and studies are complete, and customers have been approached; the capex is to be executed as a first priority once the deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. A term loan is expected in a couple of weeks to fund the open offer (Rs 151 crore) and the remaining gap. Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 50 crore capex plan consistent with the individual product items?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore and boric acid Rs 20-25 crore total about Rs 45 crore, rounded to Rs 50 crore including inflation and contingency.

qa_highlights.question: Will the open offer be tendered, and when does control transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not wait for the open offer to complete; it is using the expedited SEBI route to take control, with the open offer running in parallel. The SEBI holding period currently applies.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for unpledging Indo Borax shares pledged for the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; the pledge is standard for acquisition financing and is a work in progress.
